_doc: Which virgil/*.json sidecars hold a CITEKEY (task 615) — the census a citekey rename fans out over.
The app's rename owner is src/lib/identity/identity-cascade.ts; the skill-side owner is
apply_response.py's renameCitekey op, which re-keys EVERY file under `rekey` (one rule each,
rename_citekey.CITEKEY_REKEYERS) in the same atomic pen commit as the .tex + .bib writes.
`rekey` ∪ `notCitekeyKeyed` must equal the app's sidecar SSOT (SIDECAR_VALUE in
fails when a new sidecar is added without deciding which list it belongs to, and
editor/scripts/tests/test_rename_citekey_cascade.py fails when a rule has no Python re-keyer.

rekey.shape: { citations: [{ keys: string[], command: string }] } — keys[] and the \cite command text
V1 flat { citekey: html } (identity-cascade flag OFF, the default) or V2 { v: 2, byUid, orphanByKey } — byUid is rename-proof; orphanByKey is citekey-keyed
{ requests: [{ bibKey, entryUid? }] } — bibKey is the identity when entryUid is absent, and the human-readable mirror when present

notCitekeyKeyed.ai-requests.json: request inbox, paragraph-anchored; bib reviews live in bib-review-requests.json
notCitekeyKeyed.archive.json: archived panel cards; citation/footnote cards are refused by archive-card
notCitekeyKeyed.bib-settings.json: entryRequests[].resolvedKey is a display-only history label of what a past request produced, not an identity
notCitekeyKeyed.footnotes.json: footnote cards keyed by footnote id; a \cite inside a footnote body lives in the .tex, which the rename rewrites
notCitekeyKeyed.orphaned-footnotes.json: footnote bodies keyed by footnote id. RESIDUAL (task 615): a body's TipTap JSON may hold a citation node whose command names a citekey; neither the app cascade nor this rename re-keys it yet
